items.title: Product Owner
items.description: Are you a Product Owner with a passion for i-Gaming, innovation, and a love for improving user experiences? We're looking for a talented Product Owner to join our team in Malta and help us bring Betsson Group's vision “to provide the best customer experience in the industry” to life. The Wow As a Platform Product Owner, you will be part of a team leading the development of our in-house proprietary platform, which powers our operations across multiple customer touchpoints on an international scale. You will be assigned product responsibility for specific parts of the platform and for specific initiatives on the product roadmap. You will work closely with engineering teams, stakeholders and the wider product organisation on developing and improving the capabilities of the platform as a strategic asset for the group. What we are looking for 2+ years of working experience as a product owner or product manager. Highly skilled and experienced in collecting requirements and producing product specifications. Proven ability to prioritise and manage multiple initiatives simultaneously. Familiarity with cloud-based platforms, APIs, and data integration. Experience working in an Agile/Scrum development environment. Experience with analytics tools and metrics-driven decision making. Great if you have Relevant experience in the gaming industry and knowledgeable on the requirements of one or more jurisdictions. A technical background in software engineering. Familiarity with functional and non-functional KPIs. Experience working with platforms that serve multiple customer touchpoints. Experience working with geographically distributed development teams. Strong organisational, planning and project management skills. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. Good presentation skills. Professional working proficiency in English. A taster of what you will be involved with Act as the voice of the customer throughout the product development process. Actively lead or participate in product discovery activities (such as identifying user needs, requirements gathering, scoping and solution design). Produce detailed product specifications in the form of user stories with detailed acceptance criteria (functional and non-functional), complemented by visual aids where relevant. Clearly inform engineering teams about the work that is prioritised and why, so that they are motivated to build optimal solutions. Provide the necessary product support to the engineering teams as may be required to aid their delivery, including active participation in agile ceremonies. Actively support roadmap planning and manage deliveries from start to end, including active co-ordination with stakeholders and other teams as and when required. Ensure that the product development backlog is properly organised, prioritised, and kept up to date. Contribute to the product vision, and champion this vision with stakeholders and the engineering teams. Communicate product status, progress, and upcoming milestones to stakeholders. Hold effective presentations (including demos and trainings) with stakeholders for new product concepts and releases as and when required. Ensure that effective KPIs and data collection mechanisms are in place to understand product performance. Monitor platform performance and KPIs to identify opportunities for optimisation. Ensure that relevant product documentation and wikis are well maintained. Perform user acceptance testing of new product releases (or ensure co-ordination of). What we offer Much like riding a rollercoaster, sometimes life at Betsson can be lightning fast with twists and turns but always FUN! Then again, what else would you expect from a business 75% millennial and 1700 strong, spread across 7 offices with 900 based out of our Malta HQ alone! We recognise it may not be for the faint-hearted, but if you’re a go-getter, initiator and adrenaline junkie, always striving to push the boundaries and challenge yourself, then you’ll fit right in. Challenge accepted? By submitting your application, you understand that your personal data will be processed as set out in our Privacy Policy

items.title: Data Science Tech Lead Manager, Model Experience
items.location_text: New York City, NY; San Francisco, CA; Seattle, WA
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role As part of our growing Data Science and Analytics team, you will play an instrumental role in our company's mission of building safe and beneficial artificial intelligence by driving data-informed decision making across our organization. You bring experience from high-bar teams and are eager to help shape the norms and best practices of a growing data science team as Anthropic continues to scale. In this unique company, technology, and moment in history, your work will be critical to informing our strategy as we deploy safe, frontier AI at scale to the world. You'll be the senior data science leader for Model Experience and a strategic thought partner to product, engineering, and research leaders. Working where frontier AI research reaches the public, you'll help shape model roadmap and launch decisions, bringing a point of view on how users experience our models and what good looks like beyond benchmark scores. As a tech lead manager, you'll also hire and manage a team of data scientists, setting their agenda, personally leading the highest-stakes analyses, and raising the bar for how data shapes model and product decisions. Responsibilities: Act as a strategic thought partner to product, engineering, and research leaders, helping shape model roadmap priorities, launch decisions, and the major bets the team makes Set the data science agenda for Model Experience, deciding where the team can have the most impact on model development and launch decisions and what it should deprioritize Hire, manage, and develop a team of data scientists, coaching them to move from answering questions to shaping decisions Frame the most important and ambiguous questions about model quality and user experience, size the opportunities, and make clear recommendations, including when they challenge the current direction Define how Model Experience measures success, establishing the core metrics and measurement frameworks across external products and internal testing that align teams and leadership on what matters Set the standard for experimentation and causal inference across Model Experience, including where launches lack a clean A/B test, and personally lead the highest-stakes analyses Turn complex analyses of model and user behavior into clear narratives and recommendations that drive decisions with senior leadership and cross-functional partners Establish foundational data practices and shape the analytics infrastructure Model Experience needs to support rapid iteration and decision-making as our models and products evolve You may be a good fit if you: Have extensive experience in data science, including leading analytics for a product or research area at significant scale Have 3+ years managing data science teams, including setting team direction, hiring, and developing senior data scientists Have been a trusted partner to senior product, research, and business leaders, with clear examples of changing a roadmap or high-stakes decision Bring strong product sense and business judgment, including the ability to frame the right question and take a position with incomplete information Have deep expertise in experimental design, causal inference, and statistical modeling at high scale, with enough fluency in Python and SQL to stay hands-on and guide others' technical work Communicate clearly in writing and in presentations, including to executive audiences Have a bias for action and thrive in ambiguous, fast-moving environments where you must create clarity and drive progress Care about the company's mission of building helpful, honest, and harmless AI Strong candidates may also have: Experience with AI/ML products, large language models, or developer tools in the AI/ML ecosystem Experience as a tech lead manager or player-coach, balancing hands-on technical work with people management Experience building or scaling a data science team in a fast-growing organization Experience working closely with Product or Research teams, especially on LLM or AI products Comfort working with unstructured data The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $380,000 — $460,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

items.title: Land and Data Center Development
items.description: About the Team OpenAI’s Compute organization builds the infrastructure that powers frontier AI training and inference. This work brings together commercial, technical, strategy, and operations teams to secure and develop the sites and capacity needed for large-scale compute deployment. We partner across real estate, power, engineering, legal, finance, and delivery to connect infrastructure needs with viable development opportunities and executable commercial agreements. About the Role We’re looking for a commercial real estate (CRE) development professional to help secure land and data-center capacity for OpenAI’s compute infrastructure. This is a combined role spanning land acquisition and development, data-center leasing, and real estate acquisitions. The ideal candidate is particularly strong in land and can also contribute across data-center transactions. You’ll source and evaluate opportunities, structure and negotiate agreements, and coordinate commercial and technical diligence. Working with legal, finance, engineering, and development partners, you’ll connect transaction decisions with infrastructure requirements and carry opportunities through agreement execution and handoff. Responsibilities - Lead sourcing, evaluation, and commercial execution of land acquisition opportunities for data-center development. - Support data-center leasing and real estate acquisitions, working across land and data-center transactions as priorities require. - Build relationships with landowners, brokers, developers, and data-center counterparties to source opportunities. - Structure and negotiate land acquisition, site-control, and data-center lease agreements with legal and business partners. - Coordinate diligence with legal, finance, engineering, and development partners, translating site constraints and readiness risks into commercial decisions. - Evaluate deal economics and present clear recommendations on costs, terms, tradeoffs, and next steps. - Manage the transaction pipeline, keep stakeholders aligned, and resolve issues that affect decisions and execution. - Drive transactions through agreement execution and coordinate clear handoffs to the teams responsible for development and delivery. Qualifications - Strong commercial real estate development experience, with depth in land acquisition, site control, and development feasibility. - A record of sourcing, structuring, and negotiating complex real estate agreements. - Ability to work across land transactions and data-center leasing, with sound judgment about their different commercial and development requirements. - Sound commercial judgment and the ability to assess deal economics, identify risks, and make practical recommendations. - Experience working across legal, finance, engineering, and operations teams to move transactions forward. - Clear communication and strong ownership of complex negotiations, competing priorities, and uncertain timelines. items.title: Mechanical Lead
items.description: About the Team OpenAI's data center construction teams work with engineering, supply chain, safety, quality, commissioning and operations partners to deliver the infrastructure that supports our computing needs. Mechanical delivery brings together cooling equipment, plant, piping and controls interfaces so that systems are installed, tested and ready for commissioning. About the Role As a Mechanical Lead, you will lead mechanical field delivery for data center construction, including cooling infrastructure, mechanical yards, piping and data hall fit-out. You will oversee general contractors, specialist installers and service providers, combining practical mechanical expertise with hands-on field leadership. Your focus will be safe installation, contractor performance, coordinated interfaces and complete evidence for commissioning and operational handover. Key Responsibilities - Manage mechanical contractors, equipment and piping installers, and general-contractor interfaces against approved scope, schedule and quality requirements. - Oversee installation readiness and delivery of cooling plant, pumps, heat rejection equipment, air handling, piping and applicable liquid-cooling infrastructure. - Coordinate equipment placement, pipe routing, supports, access and maintainability with structural, electrical, controls and hardware teams. - Review contractor work plans, constructability, submittals, RFIs and change proposals; resolve field issues with the responsible engineering teams. - Oversee pressure testing, flushing, cleaning and inspection records; verify completion, defect closure and commissioning readiness. - Support commissioning specialists with mechanical startup and system tests, corrective work and complete as-built, operating and maintenance documentation. - Set contractor priorities, review staffing and progress, identify constraints early and coordinate recovery actions with construction leadership. - Maintain clear progress, risk and change reporting, with accountable handoffs between construction partners and OpenAI teams. Qualifications - Substantial mechanical construction, installation, field engineering or startup experience in data center cooling or comparable critical facilities. - Demonstrated leadership of mechanical contractors or crews, including coordination across organizations without relying on direct reporting authority. - Practical knowledge of cooling, ventilation, hydronic and pumping systems, heat rejection, piping cleanliness and vendor startup requirements. - Ability to review drawings, specifications, submittals, work methods and controls narratives for constructability and installation readiness. - Experience coordinating inspection, pressure testing, flushing, cleaning, balancing prerequisites and controls checkout. - Ability to interpret test results and deficiency records with commissioning specialists and coordinate corrective work, retesting and turnover evidence. - Clear communication and sound judgment when coordinating power, controls, startup and testing dependencies or escalating safety and delivery risks. - Relevant trade, apprenticeship, technical or degree-based preparation, or equivalent practical experience. Preferred Skills - Owner-side or specialist-contractor experience with high-density data center cooling, liquid cooling or phased cooling-system startup. - Experience with integrated systems testing, factory or site acceptance activities, and digital commissioning or field-reporting tools. - Relevant mechanical trade, controls, balancing or commissioning qualifications, or professional engineering credentials. items.title: Fire Protection Engineer
items.description: About the Team OpenAI's Industrial Compute organization delivers the infrastructure that powers frontier AI models. Within Infrastructure Delivery, we turn engineering concepts into safe, reliable, and operational AI campuses by working across design, construction, utilities, commissioning, operations, and external partners. The fire protection function establishes the life-safety and property-protection strategy for these campuses. The team connects code requirements and engineering standards to practical design, construction, testing, incident readiness, and long-term operations. About the Role We are seeking a Fire Protection Engineer to lead owner-side fire and life-safety engineering across large-scale data center programs. You will establish design criteria, review complex fire protection systems, coordinate with authorities and delivery partners, and ensure that fire and life-safety requirements remain clear from early design through construction, commissioning, and operational handover. This role requires strong technical judgment across detection, alarm, suppression, smoke control, water supply, emergency response, and code compliance. You will work closely with engineering, construction, safety, security, commissioning, and operations teams to resolve risks quickly without compromising life safety, reliability, or schedule. Key Responsibilities - Develop and maintain fire protection and life-safety design criteria, technical standards, and review requirements for self-build data center campuses. - Review fire protection drawings, specifications, code analyses, fire and life-safety narratives, hydraulic calculations, equipment submittals, and sequences of operation across all project phases. - Provide owner-side engineering direction for fire detection and alarm, automatic suppression, fire pumps and water storage, smoke control, emergency communication, and related life-safety systems. - Integrate fire protection requirements with architectural, structural, electrical, mechanical, controls, security, hardware, and operational systems. - Partner with code officials, authorities having jurisdiction, insurers, consultants, contractors, and equipment vendors to resolve code interpretations and approval risks. - Support constructability reviews, RFIs, submittals, field inspections, deficiency resolution, and change management during active construction. - Define commissioning, integrated-system testing, acceptance, turnover, and operational-readiness criteria for fire and life-safety systems. - Assess fire and life-safety risks associated with high-density compute, battery and energy-storage systems, generators and fuel systems, utility infrastructure, cooling systems, hazardous materials, and construction activities. - Support incident response, root-cause reviews, corrective actions, and lessons learned, translating operational findings into improved designs and standards. - Maintain clear records of design decisions, code positions, approvals, testing results, open risks, and turnover requirements. - Travel regularly to project sites to support design reviews, field execution, testing, commissioning, and operational readiness. Qualifications - Bachelor's degree in Fire Protection Engineering or a related engineering discipline, or equivalent practical experience delivering fire and life-safety systems. - 8+ years of fire protection engineering experience supporting data centers, industrial facilities, advanced manufacturing, energy infrastructure, or other mission-critical environments. - Strong knowledge of applicable building and fire codes and standards, including IBC, IFC, NFPA requirements, and local authority approval processes. - Technical depth in fire alarm and detection, water-based suppression, special-hazard suppression, fire pumps and water supply, smoke control, egress, and integrated life-safety systems. - Experience reviewing fire protection designs, specifications, hydraulic calculations, equipment submittals, testing procedures, and commissioning results. - Demonstrated ability to work with authorities having jurisdiction, engineering consultants, contractors, insurers, vendors, and internal stakeholders. - Experience resolving field issues and design changes while maintaining clear code compliance, safety, quality, schedule, and documentation. - Strong written and verbal communication, sound engineering judgment, and the ability to create clarity when requirements or ownership are ambiguous. - Professional Engineer licensure in Fire Protection Engineering, or the ability to obtain licensure in relevant jurisdictions. Preferred Skills - Experience with hyperscale data centers, high-density compute environments, or global multi-site infrastructure programs. - Experience with battery rooms, energy-storage systems, generator plants, fuel systems, high-voltage substations, or other campus utility infrastructure. - Familiarity with performance-based design, fire and smoke modeling, quantitative risk assessment, or fire-hazard analysis. - Experience leading integrated testing and coordinating fire alarm, suppression, controls, security, mechanical, and electrical interfaces. - Experience developing reusable standards, design templates, commissioning requirements, and incident-prevention programs across multiple sites. You will help sites meet applicable OSHA standards and other HSE requirements, from construction through commissioning and handoff to Operations. You will work across site teams, delivery partners and central functions to establish practical expectations, verify execution and turn portfolio data into action. This role combines hands-on HSE expertise with a portfolio view of contractor performance, risk and operational readiness. Key Responsibilities - Develop a consistent portfolio HSE framework covering contractor expectations, risk assessments, field verification, training and escalation, aligned with OpenAI’s EHS standards and relevant specialists. - Translate applicable OSHA construction and general-industry requirements into practical site expectations, verify implementation and clarify responsibilities as work transitions from construction to commissioning and Operations. - Partner with site and discipline leaders to assess high-risk work, verify critical controls and escalate unsafe conditions, including electrical energization, hazardous energy, lifting, excavation and concurrent construction and operating activities. - Establish portfolio performance measures and reporting for HSE outcomes, contractor performance, corrective-action closure and handoff readiness; align definitions with delivery and Operations teams and validate data quality. - Lead cross-site performance reviews to identify recurring risks, compare execution against agreed expectations and drive improvement plans with accountable owners, milestones and follow-through. - Plan risk-based site assurance and contractor reviews, support incident and near-miss investigations, verify corrective actions and embed lessons learned across the portfolio. - Coordinate environmental compliance with site teams and specialists, including waste management, spill prevention, stormwater controls and relevant permit obligations. - Define HSE readiness criteria for operational handoff with commissioning and Operations teams, including training, procedures, emergency preparedness, outstanding risks and transfer of required records. - Provide clear portfolio updates and recommendations to leadership, surface decisions and resource needs early, and build consistent safety leadership across employees, developers, contractors and service providers. Own day-to-day discipline execution and contractor performance within the assigned site scope and delegated authority. Coordinate priorities and interfaces through the Site Construction Manager; escalate material cost, schedule, design and acceptance decisions to the appropriate owners. This is a senior site delivery role, suited to an experienced superintendent, supervisor, manager or trade lead. Accountability is for an assigned discipline and site work packages. Site assignment, duration and any shared coverage follow project phase, workload and the staffing plan; effective on-site coverage is required during critical activities. Qualifications - Typically 8–10 years of large-scale data center network deployment, structured cabling, physical-layer installation or infrastructure delivery, with demonstrated field and contractor leadership. Equivalent depth of practical delivery experience will be considered. - Strong understanding of physical data center network topologies, network components, bills of materials, rack constraints and installation sequencing; translate approved designs into executable field plans. - Deep practical knowledge of fiber and copper plant installation, trunks, panels, terminations, cleaning, labeling and cable administration, including routing diversity and pathway separation. - Ability to oversee and assess port-to-port verification, continuity, optical power and optical time-domain reflectometer (OTDR) testing; items.title: Member of Technical Staff (Site Reliability Engineer, Cloud Infrastructure)
items.location_text: San Francisco, Remote (United States), Seattle, New York City
items.description: Perplexity serves hundreds of millions of queries a month. Every answer, every Perplexity Computer task, and every enterprise deployment runs on production infrastructure owned by the Cloud Infrastructure team: a fleet of Kubernetes clusters across a multi-account AWS estate, private networks that reach hyperscalers and the neoclouds serving our models, and the storage underneath our user data and agentic workloads. We're looking for SREs who treat reliability as a software problem. You'll own compute, networking, and storage at scale and keep production stable while everything built on top of it is changing fast. RESPONSIBILITIES - Own production at scale. Run the compute, networking, and storage foundation behind Perplexity's consumer, Computer, API, and enterprise products, and own its availability, latency, and cost. - Run our Kubernetes fleet. Operate and upgrade the EKS clusters that host web services, search, datastores, and secure sandboxes. Tune scheduling, autoscaling, node lifecycle, DNS, and service networking so clusters stay healthy under bursty, fast-growing load. - Engineer the network. Design and operate VPC architectures, Transit Gateway and PrivateLink connectivity, load balancing, DNS, and egress across accounts, regions, and cloud providers. - Keep data durable and fast. Own the storage layer (EBS, S3, DynamoDB, and the managed databases and caches our services depend on), including performance, durability, backups, and restores that have actually been tested. - Manage everything as code. Run infrastructure through Terraform and CI/CD. Build reusable modules and guardrails, and make every change reviewable, repeatable, and safe to roll back. - Prepare for failures. Define SLOs, build alerts that someone can act on, design for zone and regional failure, and run game days and disaster-recovery exercises that prove recovery works. - Lead incident response. Be on the critical path when things break. Drive incidents to resolution, write blameless postmortems, and land the fixes so the same failure never pages anyone twice. - Scale ahead of demand. Own capacity planning, quotas, reservations, and cost efficiency so product launches and traffic spikes never wait on infrastructure. - Automate away the toil. Build tooling, increasingly agent-driven, that turns provisioning, upgrades, and remediation into self-serve, hands-off workflows for every engineering team. QUALIFICATIONS We expect you to have real depth in most of these: - Deep AWS expertise. You know VPC, IAM, EC2, EKS, ELB, Route 53, S3, EBS, etc. well past the console, including their limits, failure modes, and the bill that comes with them. - Production Kubernetes at scale: cluster upgrades, CNI, CoreDNS, autoscalers like Karpenter, and debugging a misbehaving node at 3 a.m. Writing Helm charts alone doesn't count. - Terraform mastery. You've designed module structures, managed state across many accounts, and run large refactors and imports without taking production down. - Strong networking fundamentals (TCP/IP, DNS, TLS, load balancing, routing). - You write real code in Python, Go, or Rust for automation, tooling, and controllers, and you'd rather automate a runbook than follow it. - Fluency with observability tools like Datadog, Prometheus, or Grafana, and the judgment to turn metrics, logs, and traces into SLOs and alerts that matter. - A track record of leading production incidents and turning root-cause analysis into durable fixes. - You own problems end-to-end and do well when the path forward isn't laid out for you. ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE WE VALUE - Multi-region active-active or failover architectures, and disaster-recovery programs with real recovery targets. - Proxies, service meshes, and kernel-level networking: Envoy, Istio, Cilium, or eBPF. - GitOps and progressive delivery: Argo CD, Flux, or similar. - Enterprise and compliance environments: single-tenant or BYOC deployments, KMS/BYOK, SOC 2 or similar controls. - Running stateful systems in production: Postgres, Redis, or search engines like Vespa or Elasticsearch. - Multi-cloud or neocloud operations (GCP, CoreWeave, or similar). - FinOps: cost attribution, Savings Plans and reservations, and making infrastructure cheaper without making it fragile.

In this role, you will master a new domain of sourcing, source world-class technical talent, and influence the scaling of a high-growth Canadian tech company. If you consider yourself resilient, collaborative, influential, and a lifelong learner with an established network, we’d love to hear from you! Please Note: We have offices in Toronto, San Francisco, and London but embrace being remote-first! FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS: - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch. - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health. - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme. - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent. - Annual enrichment benefits: Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit. items.location_text: San Francisco, Remote (United States), Toronto, Seattle, New York City
items.description: Perplexity serves hundreds of millions of queries a month, and every one of them fans out into multiple AI inference requests running in real time. Behind that sits a large GPU fleet spread across several cloud providers. Today, our inference engineers and researchers build models while also managing networking, securing capacity, and operating the underlying GPU clusters, responsibilities we want a dedicated platform team to own. Your job is to take ownership of that infrastructure and hide its complexity behind a unified, self-serve platform for running training and inference workloads. RESPONSIBILITIES - Build a self-serve compute platform. Design and own the systems that let inference engineers and researchers launch training jobs and operate inference services without managing GPU provisioning, cluster configuration, or provider-specific infrastructure. - Operate the GPU fleet. Own provisioning, lifecycle management, reliability, and capacity integration across providers, giving teams a consistent way to use compute regardless of where it runs. - Solve for GPU scarcity. Build the scheduling and placement logic that finds available capacity across providers, packs it efficiently, and gets the right workload onto the right hardware under real constraints. - Support two very different workloads. Keep long-running distributed training jobs healthy while simultaneously guaranteeing the availability and latency of production inference services on the same fleet. - Own the Kubernetes for GPU orchestration. Write the operators and CRDs, and manage many clusters across providers so the platform behaves the same everywhere we run. - Make failure boring. Build the fault tolerance, autoscaling, and observability that keep the fleet utilized and let workloads survive node loss, provider hiccups, and capacity shifts without human intervention. - Set technical direction across teams. Partner with inference and cloud infrastructure engineers to turn operational constraints into a coherent platform architecture and roadmap. QUALIFICATIONS We expect you to have real depth in most of these: - Deep Kubernetes experience — custom operators, CRDs, and multi-cluster federation, not just running kubectl apply. - You've managed GPU clusters at scale: NVIDIA hardware, CUDA, and the networking that makes them fast (InfiniBand or RoCE). - You've orchestrated compute across multiple clouds (CoreWeave, AWS, GCP, or similar) and understand how different each one really is. - Strong distributed systems fundamentals: scheduling, resource allocation, and fault tolerance under load. - You write infrastructure and systems-level code in Go, Rust or C++. - You've supported both long-running training jobs and high-availability inference services, and you know why they pull infrastructure in opposite directions. - You own problems end-to-end and do well when the path forward isn't laid out for you. ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE WE VALUE - Inference serving stacks: vLLM, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM. - Slurm or other HPC schedulers. - GPU kernel work in CUDA or Triton — not required, but notable. - High-speed interconnects: InfiniBand, RoCE, or RDMA in production. - Observability for ML workloads: Prometheus, Grafana, or Weights & Biases.

items.description: Join us in building the future of finance. Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading. About the team + role We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. At Robinhood, Quality Engineering (QE) is a critical function within our broader engineering organization. We serve as the final line of defense for product quality—empowering teams to ship confidently by embedding robust test strategies, running critical end-to-end checks, and maintaining automation systems that scale with our product velocity. Our mission is to uphold a high bar for customer experience, especially during P0 launches, through a mix of technical expertise, test execution, and cross-functional collaboration. As a Senior Quality Engineer, you will support high-impact product launches by designing test strategies, executing manual and automated testing, and partnering with our contractor team on regression test cycles. This role requires someone who thrives in fast-paced environments, cares deeply about the customer experience, and is eager to shape the test infrastructure behind Robinhood’s iOS, Android, and Web apps. This role is based in our New York City, New York office(s), with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week. items.title: Motion Designer
items.description: About the Team OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood, as it leaves the lab and meets the world. This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning. About the Role OpenAI is seeking a Motion Designer to help tell the stories behind our research. You’ll translate complex ideas, emerging capabilities, and the work of our researchers into clear, engaging motion across films, launches, demos, and other communications. Working within the creative team, you’ll partner with Research, Brand, and production teams to shape work from early concepts through final delivery. You’ll help determine what a story needs visually, explore different approaches, and bring those ideas to life through thoughtful design and animation. This is a hands-on role for someone with strong motion craft, curiosity about unfamiliar subjects, and the ability to find a compelling visual approach when the brief is still taking shape. You’ll contribute to how OpenAI’s research is expressed in motion, developing original work and reusable approaches that help the team build on what it learns. In this role, you will: - Develop motion concepts for research stories, working with creative partners and subject matter experts to understand the ideas and identify how best to communicate them. - Design and produce high-quality 2D and 3D motion for research films, launches, demos, and supporting content. - Apply and extend OpenAI’s visual and motion language, balancing consistency with the needs of each story. - Take work from visual exploration, storyboards, and animatics through animation, compositing, and final delivery. - Collaborate closely with designers, filmmakers, editors, producers, and researchers, bringing a motion perspective into the creative process early. - Translate technical or abstract concepts into visual sequences that are accessible to a broad audience while preserving the meaning of the underlying work. - Work with producers to scope projects, communicate dependencies, and maintain a high standard of craft as priorities and timelines evolve. - Present work clearly, explain creative decisions, and incorporate feedback from creative and technical partners. - Develop reusable assets, templates, and workflows where they improve quality and make recurring work easier to produce. You might thrive in this role if you have: - 7+ years of experience in motion design across films, campaigns, launches, or other narrative work. - A strong portfolio demonstrating design judgment, animation craft, and the ability to carry an idea from concept through finished execution. - The ability to explore an open-ended brief, propose a clear creative direction, and refine it through collaboration. - Proficiency in After Effects and experience with Cinema 4D or comparable 3D tools, alongside editing and compositing workflows. - Comfort working in Figma and sharing work across design and production teams. - A strong understanding of typography, composition, timing, rhythm, and visual storytelling. - Experience making complex or unfamiliar subjects understandable through design and motion. - Experience working with subject matter experts and incorporating technical feedback without losing clarity or creative quality. - Curiosity about AI and research, and a willingness to learn enough about a subject to represent it thoughtfully. items.title: Senior Client Partner - US
items.location_text: New York, New York, United States
items.description: Are you ready to get the Easygo Edge? This is a rare thing in ad sales: you’ll be KICK’s first Senior Client Partner in the US. There’s no book to inherit. You’ll map the region, choose where we start and decide how KICK goes to market with agencies and advertisers, with a real say in what the product becomes. What you’ll build with us: Open the US market for KICK and own the revenue number. You’ll go beyond the media buy, into sponsorships and branded integrations campaigns. This is a full-time opportunity based in New York. You’ll work from home, but you won’t be working alone. You’ll be out in the market with agencies and advertisers, and closely connected to our Australian and Serbian teams as we build KICK’s US presence together. Who is Easygo and KICK? Easygo is a high-growth, high-velocity tech company with millions of eyeballs on us every day. We’re building the future of fearless tech. We’re the creators behind some of the most popular brands, including Stake, KICK and Easygo Games. These brands have a fierce global following, but our crew is employed directly by Easygo, and that’s where the real fun happens. KICK is our live streaming platform, built to put creators and their communities first. It gives content creators 95% of their streaming income and has redefined what a live streaming platform can be. KICK started as a disruptor challenging the status quo. Since launching in 2022, it has grown to more than 100 million accounts, and 81.7% of its audience is aged 18 to 34. Creators stream on KICK across gaming, talk shows, podcasts, IRL, sport and events. We’re always looking for people who are hungry, humble and move fast, and who are ready to Unify, Disrupt and Evolve with us. With us you’ll grow faster and go further. Your work has impact, and that gives you an edge you can’t get anywhere else. The impact you’ll make: Own and deliver KICK’s US revenue across video, display and native inventory Open the holding groups and the advertisers behind them, building trusted relationships from planning teams up to C-level Lead data driven strategy and storytelling, translating complex performance data into clear insights, recommendations, and narratives that influence senior decision makers and unlock upsell and cross sell opportunities. Build KICK’s US commercial story, using the audience, category and data-led proof points that get us onto plans Negotiate annual trading agreements, master agreements and multi-year spend commitments Own the pipeline and forecast, and grow the region year on year through retention, share of wallet and new accounts Mentor the team as it grows, and set the standard for how KICK sells in the region, and foster a culture of accountability, curiosity, collaboration, and continuous improvement. Your track record: 9+ years in digital media sales, with a proven record of owning and delivering a holding group or regional revenue number Established relationships across US agency groups, independents and key advertisers Experience negotiating trading agreements and multi-year commitments, and presenting to senior agency and client stakeholders Working knowledge of programmatic (PMPs, programmatic guaranteed, and DSP and SSP mechanics) Familiarity with CRM and order management systems (Boostr is a plus) Comfort building without an established process, in a function and region that are both being built Bonus points if you also have: Experience with creator networks, streaming, live broadcasting, entertainment or gaming platforms Relationships with programmatic buyers and brand-direct advertisers Here are our benefits and perks: Sharpening your edge The ultimate sandbox. Exciting, on-the-job learning opportunities. 1 in 3 of our people level up their roles every year. If you deliver, you move. Competitive pay and bonus scheme Market-synced pay that respects your craft and location. Performance-based bonus recognition based on your impact (up to 20%). Help us build our crew and get paid for it with our high-value referral bonus. Because great people know great people. Other perks 18 weeks of paid parental leave for primary carers, so you can be there for the moments that matter. Comprehensive medical, dental and vision coverage. Matched 401(k) contributions, so your future grows alongside your career. We play fair. We hire fair. True to our value of ‘Play fair’ we always hire fair. Our work and our brands are fuelled by our diverse culture. We hire for talent and grit. But we never discriminate. Your race, religion, nationality, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, marital, veteran, or disability status won’t affect our hiring decision, or your trajectory here. Come as you are and get the Easygo edge. #s-dni

items.title: Marketing Technology & Operations Lead, APAC
items.description: ABOUT OPENAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company committed to ensuring that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of AI capabilities while prioritizing safety, responsible deployment, and human needs. Our mission requires a team that represents a diversity of perspectives, voices, and experiences. ABOUT THE ROLE We are seeking an experienced JAPAC Marketing Operations Lead to build the operational foundations that connect regional B2B marketing activity to customer engagement, sales progression, and measurable business impact. This role serves as a critical bridge between global marketing and revenue operations and GEO B2B leaders, ensuring field leadership drives optimized customer journeys, measurement frameworks, and performance impact. It will deliver country level performance reporting and insights. Embedded in JAPAC’s GTM strategy, you will work closely with country marketing leads, GTM leaders, and Sales Operations to translate business priorities into a regional operations roadmap. You will represent JAPAC’s requirements with global Marketing Operations, ensuring that technology, data, and process decisions support local sales motions, customer journeys, and growth priorities. This is a hands-on role spanning the customer journey—from audience acquisition and database health through campaign execution, lead management, and performance reporting. You will combine technical fluency, analytical judgment, and strong cross-functional collaboration to help regional teams launch faster, improve follow-up, and understand what drives results. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES - Own the regional operations roadmap. Partner with JAPAC Marketing, GTM, and Sales Operations to consolidate country requirements, prioritize improvements against business goals, and represent regional needs in global MarkOps planning. - Manage regional marketing technology operations. Oversee the regional use of marketing automation, CRM, and event and webinar platforms. Work with global MarkOps and systems teams to troubleshoot issues, improve integrations, and validate changes across markets. - Build a healthier, more actionable database. Partner with GTM on priority-account and contact acquisition, enrichment, segmentation, and data quality. Improve opt-in coverage and marketability while maintaining appropriate consent and data-handling practices. - Own campaign setup, lead management, and sales handoffs. Set up and quality-check campaigns in marketing automation and CRM systems, including audience lists, registration forms, campaign tracking, and lead-capture workflows. Ensure leads from field events, webinars, and other campaigns enter the agreed qualification and routing processes. Work with Sales Operations, AEs, and SDRs to conduct regular reviews of untouched marketing-qualified leads (MQLs) and resolve routing or follow-up gaps. - Connect the customer journey. Work with regional marketers and global MarkOps to connect acquisition, engagement, nurture, and sales touchpoints, making relevant customer signals available to the teams that need to act on them. - Standardize campaign execution. Develop reusable templates, workflows, and quality checks that help field marketers launch campaigns quickly and consistently, with documented adaptations for local requirements. - Partner with Legal/Privacy and global MarkOps to embed market-specific data privacy and regulatory requirements across JAPAC into consent management, audience acquisition, campaign execution, and data handling. - Measure campaign performance and impact. Establish reliable reporting for field programs, local events, webinars, and account-based marketing. Apply shared measurement and attribution definitions to assess engagement, conversion, pipeline contribution, and ROI where the data supports it. - Enable regional teams. Train marketers on tools, campaign processes, data quality, and applicable privacy and compliance requirements. Provide practical support during JAPAC working hours and coordinate specialist guidance where needed. Partner with Sales Operations to jointly enable GTM teams on lead follow-up processes, ownership, and service-level agreements (SLAs). - Improve automation and operating efficiency. Identify repetitive work and partner with global teams to introduce dependable automation and AI-enabled workflows that reduce manual handoffs and improve execution. QUALIFICATIONS - 10+ years of experience in B2B marketing operations, marketing technology, revenue operations, or a closely related function. - Hands-on experience with marketing automation and CRM platforms, including Marketo and Salesforce, Adobe Experience Platform and familiarity with event or webinar technology. - Demonstrated experience improving database quality, segmentation, lead lifecycle processes, scoring, routing, and marketing-to-sales handoffs. - Strong analytical skills, with experience in campaign reporting, funnel analysis, attribution, and translating findings into operational improvements. - Experience supporting multiple markets and balancing global standards with regional business requirements. - Proven ability to work closely with Marketing, GTM, Sales Operations, and technical teams, influencing priorities and driving work through to completion. - Sound judgment around consent, customer data, privacy, and operational quality. NICE TO HAVE - Experience supporting JAPAC markets, including local campaign execution and collaboration across languages and time zones. - Experience with ABM, buying-group engagement, and enterprise, developer, or startup audiences. - Familiarity with data integrations, APIs, and customer engagement or product-usage signals. - Practical experience building or improving AI-enabled workflows and automation. We're a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. The CXR Pathway Program is a paid program that launches your career in financial services. You'll be paid while you study for your SIE, Series 7 and Series 63 licenses and learn the job through hands-on, on-the-job training. You'll build foundational knowledge and confidence alongside your cohort, and finish the program ready to become a registered broker (Registered Representative). Learn by doing, from day one. We are looking for recent graduates who have customer-facing experience and are interested in becoming a Registered Representative through Robinhood's licensing and training program. items.title: Global Procurement Analyst
items.description: We are an AI company operating at the cutting edge of the industry, growing quickly in a fast-moving environment. As we scale and prepare for a future IPO, we are building our Procurement function from the ground up. This is our first Procurement Analyst role in the company, so you will help define how we buy, not just execute it. Your passion for Procurement will help build and run our source-to-pay processes with strong internal controls, clear segregation of duties between procurement and payment, and audit-ready documentation. This is a global role: you will support stakeholders and suppliers across regions and work closely with the rest of the Procure to Pay (P2P) and Finance teams. Key Responsibilities Procurement operations Manage the end-to-end purchasing operations across all spend categories (software, cloud, professional services, hardware, facilities, and more), from requisition intake and PO issuance in Zip / Coupa. Review purchase requests for completeness, budget and policy compliance before approval. Issue and track purchase orders, and follow up with suppliers on delivery, pricing, and service levels. Support RFQ/RFP processes: gather requirements, solicit/compare bids, and document selection rationale. Support negotiations and renewals in partnership with Legal and business owners. Support requesters across time zones and regions, handling multi-currency and cross-border purchasing needs. Controls and audit readiness Help design and implement procurement policies, approval matrices (delegation of authority), and procedures aligned with IPO and audit requirements. Enforce segregation of duties between procurement (requisition, sourcing, PO creation, vendor selection) and payment (invoice processing, payment execution), in coordination with Accounts Payable and Finance. Maintain complete, organized documentation for every purchase (quotes, approvals, contracts, POs) so it is available for internal and external audits. Monitor and report on policy exceptions, such as off-contract spend, retroactive POs, and split purchases, and escalate as needed. Support internal and external audit requests and help remediate findings. Vendor management Maintain accurate vendor master data and a centralized vendor and contract repository. Run supplier onboarding, including due diligence, documentation, tax compliance validation, and conflict-of-interest checks for domestic and international suppliers. Track supplier performance and support periodic vendor reviews using AI and other tools. Analysis and reporting Use AI to analyze spend data across categories and regions to identify savings opportunities, consolidation potential, and compliance gaps. Build regular reports and KPIs, such as spend under management, PO compliance, cycle times, and savings. Support budget tracking with Finance and flag potential overruns. Process improvement Contribute to the implementation and optimization of procurement tools and workflows, particularly Coupa and Zip. Document processes and create guidance and training for internal requesters. Propose and drive improvements that balance speed with control in a high-growth environment. Requirements Experience and knowledge 3+ years of experience in Procurement, Purchasing, or a related P2P function. Hands-on experience with Coupa and Zip or other modern procurement and AP tools. Familiarity with corporate procurement policies, guidelines, and internal controls. Understanding of P2P cycle and basic concepts of segregation of duties and approval workflows. Professional fluency in English (written and spoken), as you will primarily support global teams and suppliers. Core competencies (non-negotiable) Interpersonal skills: builds trusted relationships with stakeholders at all levels and can say “no” or “not like this” constructively. Strong negotiation and influencing skills. Communication skills: communicate clearly, in English writing and verbally, with business teams, suppliers, and senior leaders, and can explain the “why” behind controls. Ownership and a bias for action in an ambiguous, fast-changing environment. Strong attention to detail and a commitment to compliance and integrity. Self-management and strong written communication in a remote, cross-time-zone setting. Nice to have Experience in a high-growth, technology, or SaaS/AI company. Exposure to SOX, IPO readiness, or audit-ready environments. Familiarity with international supplier onboarding and tax documentation (e.g., W-8/W-9, VAT), and knowledge of EU, Mexican (CFDI, SAT compliance) as well as other government’s requirements. Bachelor’s degree in Business, Supply Chain, Finance, Industrial Engineering, or a related field. What Success Looks Like (first 6 to 12 months) Procurement policy and approval matrix adopted and followed by the business. Clear, enforced separation between procurement and payment activities. A centralized, audit-ready record for all purchases and vendors. Improved PO compliance and visibility into company spend. Positive feedback from business stakeholders on the speed and clarity of the purchasing process. PLEASE NOTE: Our policy requires a 90-day waiting period before reconsidering candidates for the same role. This allows us to ensure a fair and thorough evaluation of all applicants. About Us: At Scale, our mission is to develop reliable AI systems for the world's most important decisions. This is a field-oriented electrical & mechanical engineering role, not a traditional facilities operations position. You will combine deep systems understanding in data center power and cooling systems to aid in SOO, design, maintenance & operability, troubleshooting and other engineering related responsibility around key equipment. The role will include leveraging training and experience to establish standards, develop people, coordinate vendors, and drive issues from design, first principles, first signals through verified resolution. Remote - travel 50% Key Responsibilities - Lead field support for startup, commissioning, troubleshooting, repair, and reliability improvement across critical data center infrastructure. - Serve as the senior technical owner for transformers, switchgear, UPS systems, generators, PDUs, protection and controls, chillers, cooling towers, pumps, CDUs, CRAH units, and associated control systems. - Diagnose complex failures across power, cooling, controls, and hardware interfaces; distinguish symptoms from root causes and drive corrective actions through validation. - Build the field service operating model, including staffing recommendations, coverage, escalation paths, response expectations, spare-parts strategy, documentation, and performance metrics. - Aid in hiring, development, and coaching other field service engineers and technicians while creating a culture of safety, technical rigor, accountability, and continuous learning. - Partner with design, construction, commissioning, site operations, and hardware teams to improve maintainability, readiness, and lifecycle reliability. - Manage OEM and service-provider relationships, technical escalations, repair plans, warranties, and sustained corrective action. - Establish and improve safe work practices, including lockout/tagout, switching and maintenance procedures, MOPs, SOPs, EOPs, and incident response. - Translate field learning into design feedback, preventive maintenance improvements, training, and reusable standards. items.description: About the Team OpenAI’s Product & Research Communications team helps people understand our technology, what it makes possible, and how to use it. We work closely with teams across the company to bring new products and research to the world, tell stories grounded in real experiences, and build trusted relationships with journalists. About the Role We’re looking for a Consumer Product Communications Lead to shape how people understand and experience ChatGPT and OpenAI’s consumer-facing products. You’ll lead product communications strategy, launches, and proactive campaigns, and manage the agency partner supporting this work. You’ll develop a clear narrative for our consumer products and bring it to life through compelling launches, useful demonstrations, and stories about how people use AI in their everyday lives. You’ll build momentum between announcements, finding fresh ways to reach new audiences while earning the trust of the people who use our products most deeply. This role calls for a hands-on communications leader with strong editorial judgment, creative ambition, and the ability to turn ideas into results. You’ll have a clear point of view, work with substantial autonomy, and build close partnerships across the company. In this role, you will: - Own the communications strategy and narrative for ChatGPT and consumer-facing products, connecting product developments to what matters to users. - Lead product launches from strategy through execution, including positioning, messaging, media outreach, spokesperson preparation, and follow-through. - Develop proactive campaigns that show how people use our products to learn, create, and solve everyday problems. - Partner closely with Product, Research, Engineering, Marketing, Design, Legal, and other communications teams to shape plans, resolve tradeoffs, and communicate accurately. - Build relationships with consumer and technology journalists, creators, and other voices who help people understand new technology. - Direct the consumer communications agency partner, setting priorities, writing clear briefs, giving useful feedback, and holding the team accountable for quality and results. - Write and edit launch materials, pitches, talking points, and other communications with a high standard for clarity, accuracy, and originality. - Anticipate questions and concerns, bring audience feedback into planning, and assess whether campaigns improve understanding and earn trust. You can explain why a story, demo, or campaign will resonate and make the work better through specific feedback. - Take initiative, make sound decisions independently, and stay organized in a fast-moving environment. - Have experience managing agency partners and getting excellent work from a combined internal and external team. - Understand consumer media and culture, care about the experience of early adopters and power users, and are curious about how AI is changing people’s lives. items.title: Head of Stunt Marketing
items.description: ABOUT POLYMARKET Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market platform. We enable individuals to express views on real-world events by trading on outcomes across politics, economics, sports, culture, and current affairs. Built as a peer-to-peer marketplace with no centralized "house," Polymarket aggregates diverse opinions into transparent, market-based probabilities that reflect collective expectations about the future. We're growing fast, both in terms of volume ($21B traded in 2025) and adoption as an alternative news source. Our ambition is to become a ubiquitous beacon of truth in global media and we need your help adding fuel to the fire. ABOUT THE ROLE Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market, and sports is one of our biggest categories. The marketing team is small and moves fast. We don't have a big agency on retainer or a traditional campaign calendar. What we have is a platform that sits at the intersection of sports, news, and money, and a mandate to make the world aware of it in ways that actually stick. This role exists because guerilla and stunt marketing is one of the highest-leverage things we can do, and we need a dedicated person who owns it end to end. You'll be the one watching the game, spotting the moment, and showing up with something that earns press and goes viral, not because it was planned six months out, but because you moved faster than everyone else. The person who held this role before built a real playbook here. Your job is to run it, expand it, and make it yours. This is a high-ownership, high-visibility role. You'll work closely with the marketing lead and have real autonomy, but you'll also be expected to operate independently in the field, often on short notice. If you need a lot of structure or sign-off to act, this isn't the right fit. If you thrive on finding the moment and executing before it passes, keep reading. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Identify stunt and activation concepts tied to live sports moments, news cycles, and cultural events, then pitch them fast with a clear point of view on why they'll land - Execute on-the-ground activations at stadiums, arenas, sports bars, and public venues, handling logistics, talent, materials, and timing yourself - Monitor social media and sports news in real time to spot openings for reactive content or physical activations before the moment passes - Coordinate all logistics for guerilla campaigns from concept through execution, including permits, vendors, travel, and on-site management - Build and maintain a pipeline of stunt ideas across the major sports calendar so the team is never starting from zero - Track campaign performance after each activation, pulling together data on reach, press pickups, social engagement, and earned media to inform what comes next - Represent Polymarket in the field in a way that reflects the brand, sharp, credible, and worth paying attention to WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - 5 or more years of experience in guerilla marketing, experiential marketing, or stunt-based brand work, with specific examples of campaigns you personally executed - A real track record of viral moments, not just campaigns that got approved, but things that actually spread and earned press coverage - High sports IQ across major American leagues, NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, and college sports, with enough fluency to know which moments matter and why - Demonstrated ability to execute independently in the field, you've shown up somewhere with a plan and made it happen without a team of ten behind you - Comfort operating on short timelines, some of the best opportunities here will have a 24 to 48 hour window - (Plus) Existing relationships with sports journalists, beat reporters, or media personalities who cover games and culture - (Plus) Experience at a sports betting, DFS, or prediction market brand - (Plus) Familiarity with crypto or web3 environments and audiences BENEFITS - Competitive salary & equity - Unlimited PTO - Full Health, Vision, & Dental coverage - 401k match - Hardware setup: new MacBook Pro, big display, & accessories PAY TRANSPARENCY Base salary range: $240,000 to $260,000, plus equity and benefits. This is a good-faith range for the level we're hiring at. Experience varies widely within a title here, so if your expectations fall outside it, reach out anyway. We're always happy to talk it through.

items.description: ABOUT MISTRAL Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. The Role As an IP Rights Manager on the IP & Licensing team, you will own the operational backbone of how Mistral manages rights, obligations, and restrictions across the datasets we license. This role sits at the intersection of copyright, data protection, and AI, and exists because the volume and complexity of our data agreements have outgrown manual processes. You will work closely with the colleagues who negotiate our agreements commercially and legally, translating their work into systems, workflows, and databases that keep us compliant and scalable. The IP & Licensing team is responsible for all content and data licensing at Mistral. Your work will directly determine whether we can use the data we acquire, how we track what we are allowed to do with it, and whether our clients and partners stay within the rights we grant them. You will build the infrastructure that makes legal analysis repeatable, not just advisory. Your scope spans the full lifecycle of data-related agreements: clearing inbound data usage requests, codifying contract terms into structured metadata, tracking ongoing compliance obligations, and automating reporting. You will also design and run AI-powered workflows that handle contract review assistance, obligation extraction, and renewal alerts, turning legal judgment into scalable operations. What You Will Do - Clear inbound data usage requests by researching rights status, scope, obligations, and restrictions before data enters Mistral systems. - Review data-related agreements and codify their key terms into structured metadata, maintaining the team's template library and playbook alongside Legal. - Determine whether specific AI use cases are covered by third-party agreements, identify gaps, and recommend contract amendments. - Build and maintain a central database as the single source of truth for every signed data-related agreement, covering permitted uses, confidentiality, and re-use permissions. - Track ongoing compliance obligations and automate reporting, including renewal alerts and master licensing partnership administration. - Develop and run AI workflows for contract review assistance, obligation extraction, and compliance monitoring. - Verify provenance, ownership, and consents for acquired data, flagging obligations that must be tracked. - Monitor that Mistral clients and partners operate within granted rights, administering the approval system that enforces legal restrictions. What We're Looking For - A bachelor's degree in law, publishing, information science, business, or a related field. - 2 to 5 years of experience in copyright, permissions, licensing, legal operations, or contract administration, ideally in an AI, tech, or data-driven environment. - Solid working knowledge of EU and US copyright law and contract administration, with demonstrated ability to interpret contracts independently. - Strong attention to detail and discretion when handling confidential agreements. - Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain legal constraints to non-lawyers. - A legal-ops mindset: you take initiative, anticipate needs through ambiguity, and think about how to operationalize legal analysis at scale. - Comfort building agentic AI workflows in a complex enterprise environment; you are an AI power user, not just a consumer. - Fluency in French, German, Spanish, or another European language is a plus, as is experience with CLM tools like Ironclad, prior work setting up AI workflows in a legal team, or contracting experience with publishing houses. WHAT WE OFFER We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks. For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page https://app.notion.com/p/mistralai/Benefits-at-Mistral-36e6ba59a7fe836b93dd01737fcc27ef?source=copy_link. PRIVACY POLICY Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy https://legal.mistral.ai/terms/applicant-privacy-policy.
